'''Cristiane de Morais Smith Lehner''' is a Brazilian [[Theoretical physics|theoretical physicist]] and professor at the Institute for Theoretical Physics at the [[University of Utrecht]], where she leads a research group studying [[condensed matter]] physics, [[Ultracold atom|cold atoms]] and [[Strongly correlated material|strongly-correlated systems]]. In 2019, the [[European Physical Society]] awarded Morais Smith its [[Emmy Noether]] Distinction.<ref name="EPS_prize"/>

Morais Smith has authored or co-authored over 100 academic papers, including articles in ''[[Nature Communications]]'', ''[[Physical Review]]'', and ''[[Physical Review B]]'', where several of her papers have been recognized as "Editors Choice" and "Scientific Highlights".<ref name="CV">{{cite web|url=http://www.staff.science.uu.nl/~morai101/pdf_files/CV-Smith-Short-2018.pdf|title=Curriculum Vitae|website=uu.nl}}</ref>
As of March 2020, her work has received over 2900 citations.<ref name="google_scholar">{{cite web |title=C. M. Smith |url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=F2HOXmAAAAAJ&hl=en |website=Google Scholar |access-date=10 March 2020}}</ref>

In addition, Morais Smith is an editor for the ''[[European Physical Journal B|European Journal of Physics B]]'', which focuses on condensed matter and complex systems.<ref name="epj_b">{{cite web |title=Editorial Board |url=https://epjb.epj.org/epjb-editorial-board |website=European Journal of Physics |access-date=19 April 2019}}</ref>

==Education==
Morais Smith obtained a physics BSc from [[University of Campinas]] in 1985, continuing to complete a MSc with highest honors in 1989 entitled ''The Effect of the Initial Preparation to Describe the Dynamics of a Quantum Brownian Particle'', under her adviser [[Amir Caldeira]]. 
She continued with Caldeira to complete a PhD in 1994, also at [[University of Campinas]] entitled ''Quantum and Classical Creep of Vortices Intrinsically Pinned in High-Temperature Superconductors''. 
Much of the work for her PhD was completed at [[ETH Zurich]] where she worked with Gianni Blatter.

==Career==
Starting in March 1986, Morais Smith was a French language teacher at [[Telebrás|Brazilian Telecommunications Company (TELEBRAS)]] in Campinas Brazil, until December 1988, when she briefly became the owner of and teacher at a French language school.<ref name="CV" />

From 1989 to 1994, during her PhD, Morais Smith accepted a permanent lecturer position in the Department of Physics at the [[São Paulo State University]]  (UNESP) in [[Bauru]], Brazil.<ref name="CV" />
During this time, she was also a visiting scientist in the Condensed Matter group at the [[International Center for Theoretical Physics]] in [[Trieste]], Italy, as well as a guest PhD student at [[ETH Zurich]].<ref name="CV" />

Following the award of her PhD, she accepted a postdoctoral position at the Institute of Theoretical Physics, also at [[ETH Zurich]].<ref name="CV" />
In 1995, she moved to the Institute of Theoretical Physics at the [[University of Hamburg]], Germany as a research assistant.<ref name="hamburg">{{cite web|url=https://theorie.physnet.uni-hamburg.de/former.html|title=Former Members|website=uni-hamburg.de|access-date=2019-04-19|archive-date=2019-04-19|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190419021506/https://theorie.physnet.uni-hamburg.de/former.html}}</ref> 
After finishing a post-doc in Hamburg, Morais Smith began working at the Institute of Theoretical Physics at the [[University of Fribourg]], Switzerland, where the [[Swiss National Science Foundation]] awarded her the Professor Boursier Fellowship. At the University of Fribourg, she advanced to an associate professor position.<ref name="DresselhausRecip"/>

In 2004, Morais Smith was hired by the [[Utrecht University]] as a full professor with a chair in condensed matter theory.<ref name="DresselhausRecip">{{Cite web|url=https://www.cui-archiv.uni-hamburg.de/wp-content/uploads/2012/09/2019_03_MD-Preis_engl_fin.pdf|title=Mildred Dresselhaus Award and Recipients|date=2019|website=University of Hamburg|access-date=January 1, 2020|quote=After holding a C1 postdoc position in Hamburg, Germany, she was awarded the Professor Boursier Fellowship from the Swiss National Science Foundation and became associate professor in Fribourg, Switzerland. Finally, in 2004 she was offered a Chair in Condensed Matter Theory and became a full professor at the Institute for Theoretical Physics of Utrecht University, the Netherlands. In 2008, she was awarded the prestigious VICI fellowship from the Dutch Research Organization (NWO), which has strongly boosted her research.}}</ref> She is chair of the Condensed Matter Physics department there.<ref>[https://www.uu.nl/staff/CdeMoraisSmith UU staff page for "Prof. dr. C. (Cristiane) de Morais Smith"]</ref>

Morais Smith is one of three directors of the Delta Institute for Theoretical Physics (a collaboration between University of Amsterdam, Leiden University, and Utrecht University), where she represents Utrecht University.<ref name="delta_exec">{{cite web |title=Executive Board |url=https://www.d-itp.nl/about/organisation/executive-board/executive.html |website=Delta Institute for Theoretical Physics |date=31 October 2017 |access-date=19 April 2019}}</ref><ref name="CV" />

==Other==
Morais Smith grew up in [[Paraguaçu Paulista]], a village 500&nbsp;km from [[São Paulo]], Brazil. She was thirteen years old when she decided to become a physicist.<ref name="SNF_Horizonte">{{Cite web |url=http://www.snf.ch/SiteCollectionDocuments/horizonte/Horizonte_gesamt/Horizonte_60_D.pdf |title=Christiane de Morais Smith Lehner: Theoretische Physik im Stile Picassos|last=Dessibourg |first=Olivier |work=Horizonte |quote=Paraguaçu Paulista, ein Dorf, 500 Kilometer von São Paulo entfernt. Christiane de Morais Smith Lehner ist 13 Jahre alt, als der Lehrer seine Klasse vor eine – seiner Ansicht nach – unlösbare Aufgabe stellt. «Doch ich habe die Lösung gefunden», erzählt sie, noch immer voller Stolz. (Paraguaçu Paulista, a village 500 kilometers from São Paulo. Christiane de Morais Smith Lehner is 13 years old when the teacher presents his class with what he believes is an unsolvable task. "But I found the solution," she says, still full of pride.) |date=2004 |access-date=January 3, 2020}}</ref> She is fluent in Portuguese (her native language), English, French, Italian, German, Spanish, and Dutch.<ref name="CV" />

In September 2002, Morais Smith married [[Stefan Lehner]], a Swiss designer.<ref name="CV" />

Morais Smith was featured in a Dutch newspaper article in 2018 for her work on [[Chirality (physics)|chiral]] [[superconductors]] where the pairing function has a chirality e.g. <math>p_x + ip_y</math>. In layered chiral superconductors there is a geometric Meissner effect,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Kvorning|first1=T.|last2=Hansson|first2=T. H.|last3=Quelle|first3=A.|last4=Smith|first4=C. Morais|date=2018-05-25|title=Proposed Spontaneous Generation of Magnetic Fields by Curved Layers of a Chiral Superconductor|journal=Physical Review Letters|language=en|volume=120|issue=21|article-number=217002 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.120.217002 |pmid=29883131 |arxiv=1709.00482 |bibcode=2018PhRvL.120u7002K |s2cid=47004151 }}</ref> which is a variation on the [[Meissner effect]].

==Honors and awards==

In 2001, Morais Smith was awarded a "Professeur Boursier du Fond National Suisse" or [[Swiss National Science Foundation]] Professorship for a project entitled ''Spontaneous formation of charge patterns in two-dimensional strongly interacting electron systems''. 
<ref name="snsf_prof_awards">{{cite web |title=SNSF Professorships |url=http://www.snf.ch/SiteCollectionDocuments/fop_awa_pfs_zusprachen_2018.pdf |website=Swiss National Science Foundation |access-date=20 April 2019}}</ref><ref name="vicom_16">{{cite web |title=ViCoM Young Researchers Meeting 2016 Invited Speakers |url=https://www.sfb-vicom.at/events/young-researchers-meeting-2016/invited-speakers/ |website=Vienna Computational Materials Laboratory |access-date=19 April 2019}}</ref> 
This prize is awarded to only 2 or 3 researchers per year, and holds a monetary award of more than one million [[Swiss Francs]].<ref name="CV" />

Morais Smith received a [[People's Republic of China]] 'High-End Foreign Expert' Professorship in 2014 and 2015 at the Wilczek Quantum Center, awarded by the State Administration of Foreign Experts Affairs.<ref name="CV" />

In 2016, the [[Hamburg Centre for Ultrafast Imaging]] (CUI) awarded its [[Hamburg Centre for Ultrafast Imaging#Awardees Mildred Dresselhaus Award|Dresselhaus Prize]] to Morais Smith for "her outstanding contribution to the understanding of topological phases in two-dimensional atomic and electronic systems".<ref name="dresselhaus_prize">{{cite web|url=https://www.d-itp.nl/shared-content/news/news/2017/00/201701-dresselhaus-award-2016.html|title=Mildred Dresselhaus award for Cristiane Morais Smith|website=Delta Institute for Theoretical Physics}}</ref><ref name ="Dresselhaus">{{Cite web|url=https://www.cui-archiv.uni-hamburg.de/en/2017/01/a-jewel-of-equal-opportunities/|title=A Jewel of Equal Opportunities {{!}} CUI – The Hamburg Centre for Ultrafast Imaging|quote=Prof. Andreas Hemmerich called Morais Smith a perfect role model and his favorite proof against gravity. In his honorary speech, he outlined her path of life starting in a small village in Brazil to her engagement as a highly acclaimed physics professor at the University of Utrecht in the Netherlands.|website=www.cui-archiv.uni-hamburg.de|access-date=2020-01-02}}</ref>

In 2019, the [[European Physical Society]] awarded Morais Smith its EPS Emmy Noether Distinction "for her outstanding contributions to the theory of condensed matter systems and ultracold atoms to unveil novel quantum states of matter."<ref name="EPS_prize">{{cite web|url=http://www.epsnews.eu/2019/12/the-winter-2019-eps-emmy-noether-distinction-for-women-in-physics-is-awarded-to-cristiane-morais-smith/|title=EPS Emmy Noether distinction award for Cristiane Morais Smith|last=Bergé|first=Luc|date=16 December 2019|website=EPS|quote=Cristiane Morais Smith leads a research group in Strongly Correlated Systems at the Institute for Theoretical Physics of Utrecht University, working on low-dimensional systems, ranging from condensed matter to cold atoms. Her group pioneered the development of a thermodynamic description of topological insulators and superconductors, as well as the use of a projected quantum electrodynamics formulation to investigate topological phases driven by interactions. In the last years, her group has been playing an important role in the development of electronic quantum simulators and metamaterials in collaboration with experimentalists in Utrecht.|access-date=1 January 2020}}</ref> The EPS Emmy Noether Distinction for Women in Physics, established in 2013, is awarded "to enhance the recognition of noteworthy women physicists with a strong connection to Europe through nationality or work," particularly those who are "role models that will help to attract women to a career in physics."<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.eps.org/page/distinction_prize_en|title=EPS Emmy Noether Distinction for Women in Physics - European Physical Society (EPS)|website=www.eps.org|access-date=2020-01-02}}</ref>
